title: Burial facing the qiblah
hookLine: quickly, facing the qiblah, in the earth

lines: A BODY, AND NO IDEA WHAT TO DO.
A GRAVE, LEARNED FROM A BIRD.
cards: A burial in the Qur'an begins in the worst way. In surah al-Ma'idah, one of Adam's two sons has killed his brother, and he stands there with the body and no idea what to do with it. Then Allah sends a raven.
The bird scratches at the ground, digging, and the killer watches. He cries out in shame, in paraphrase, that he couldn't even manage what this raven manages: to cover his brother.
So a grave in the Qur'an is dug by someone learning from a bird.

teach.b: Start with the speed. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, tells people to hurry with the funeral.
His reasoning, in paraphrase: if the one who died was good, you're bringing them toward good; if not, it's a weight you set down from your shoulders.
So the washing, the shroud and the prayer come quickly, and the burial follows close behind. Grief doesn't get to wait for everything to be perfect. Then the direction.

Every day of a Muslim's life, the prayer faced one place: the qiblah, toward the Ka'bah in Makkah. In the grave, as the jurists describe it, the body is laid on its right side, the face turned that same way.
A whole life of turning one way, and it doesn't stop at the end. And then the earth. Muslim burial is in the ground itself, plainly, in the white shroud, and mourners may help fill the grave by hand.
Some communities recite a verse from surah Ta Ha at that moment, in Pickthall's translation: "Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time."
From the earth, back to the earth, out of it again.

teach.h: FROM IT, TO IT, OUT OF IT AGAIN.
teach.b: In the verse, the ground isn't the end of the sentence. It's the comma.

how: Muslims bury the dead soon after death, in the earth, wrapped in the shroud and laid on the right side facing the qiblah; mourners help fill the grave, and some communities recite Qur'an 20:55 as they do.

games.q: what does “burial facing the qiblah” mean?
o: a tomb raised so mourners at the grave can face Makkah
the body laid in the earth on its right side, facing Makkah
the body laid on its back, with its feet toward the sunrise

p: showed how to cover a body
faced in prayer, and in the grave
from it, to it, out of it again

s: the Prophet told people to wait before a funeral until everything is ready
in al-Bukhari he tells them to hurry with the funeral.
in the grave, the body is laid facing the qiblah
on its right side, as the jurists describe it, facing the direction of prayer.
the Qur'an's verse in Ta Ha speaks only of returning to the earth
it has three movements: created from it, returned to it, brought out of it again.

games.q: you're Adam's son, standing with your brother's body. a raven lands and starts to dig. what do you do?
o: watch, and learn to cover him.
games.why: in al-Ma'idah he watches the raven and learns, and cries out in shame that a bird knew more than he did.

practice: Let your weight settle into the chair or the floor, and notice the ground holding you up, as it has every day of your life without being asked.

Bring to mind soil you know, a garden, a park, a field, and hold the line from Ta Ha for a breath or two: from it, back to it, out of it again. If you pray, you can remember someone who has already been returned to the earth.

wordCard.voice: Burial facing the qiblah. The body laid in the earth, on its right side, facing the same direction it faced in prayer, and done without delay. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the direction faced in prayer, toward the Ka'bah.

carryVoice: Your line: back to the earth. From it, to it, and out of it again. Tomorrow, three days.

sources.q: Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time.
